publish.title: Ser or estar? The difference in 40 seconds
publish.description: Spanish to be: what each verb is for, with examples and a memory trick.

scenes.headline: Ser or estar? Learn the difference in seconds
scenes.narration: Spanish has two verbs for to be, and choosing between them trips up every learner.

scenes.headline: Two verbs
scenes.narration: Ser is for what something is: identity, origin, time. Estar is for how or where something is: mood and place.

left.label: Ser
left.text: What it is: identity, origin, time

right.label: Estar
right.text: How or where it is: mood, place

scenes.headline: Four examples
scenes.narration: Soy estudiante means I am a student. Estoy cansado means I am tired. Es de Madrid means he is from Madrid. Está en casa means he is at home.
items: Soy estudiante: I am a student
Es de Madrid: he is from Madrid
Está en casa: he is at home

scenes.headline: Same word, new meaning
scenes.narration: Some adjectives change meaning. With ser, aburrido means boring. With estar, it means bored.

scenes.headline: Make three sentences
scenes.narration: Write one sentence with ser and one with estar, then say them out loud.
